documents.text: Mount Everest is the highest mountain above sea level, with a height of about 8,849 metres. It lies on the border between Nepal and China.
At standard sea-level atmospheric pressure, pure water boils at 100 degrees Celsius.
Hamlet is a tragedy written by William Shakespeare, believed to have been written between about 1599 and 1601.
Apollo 11 landed on the Moon on 20 July 1969. Neil Armstrong was the first person to walk on the Moon.
James Watson and Francis Crick proposed the double helix structure of DNA in 1953.
The Python programming language was created by Guido van Rossum and first released in 1991.
Canberra is the capital city of Australia. Sydney is the country's largest city but not its capital.
World War II ended in 1945, with Germany surrendering in May and Japan in September.
Marie Curie won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1903 and the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1911.
The speed of light in a vacuum is about 299,792 kilometres per second.
The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest of Earth's oceans.
Mount Fuji is the highest mountain in Japan, at 3,776 metres.
The chemical symbol for gold is Au.
Mitochondria produce most of the chemical energy a cell needs, in the form of ATP.
The Earth orbits the Sun once about every 365.25 days.
